title: Support ticket lifecycle, SLA, test visibility, and dedupe integrity

phases.objective: Prevent cross-context and concurrent duplicate creation, classify test records from trusted evidence, calculate milestone-aware SLA, and persist ticket integrity atomically.

e2e_journeys.terminal_outcome: Ticket creation uses a transaction-held canonical dedupe claim and atomic integrity persistence; the tenant inbox returns only customer-safe fields, excludes trusted internal tests, and orders records by ticket or lifecycle-event activity.
steps: Resolve one unambiguous active tenant membership.
Build the v2 dedupe identity from tenant, user, type, capability, resource, relationship, intended parent, test classification, environment, and visibility.
Verify migration 1042 columns and the durable dedupe-claim table before mutation.
Begin one transaction and acquire the unique tenant-plus-dedupe claim row with FOR UPDATE.
Create or append the ticket and persist integrity fields in the same transaction.
Choose an integrity-ready or genuinely pre-migration-safe read projection.
List only the requesting user's or workspace-shared customer-safe records without internal tests and order them by latest ticket or lifecycle-event activity.
assertions: Different parent tickets and target capabilities produce different dedupe keys.
Production, test, environment, and visibility contexts cannot dedupe onto one another.
Two concurrent requests for one canonical identity serialize on the same database claim; one creates and the other appends after commit.
Commit and rollback release the transaction-held dedupe coordination.
Multiple active memberships require an explicit tenant_id instead of selecting the first candidate.
Schema-not-ready creation fails before ticket mutation.
Integrity persistence failure rolls back ticket creation or dedupe append and its claim lock.
Completed response and triage milestones do not create false SLA breaches.
Ordinary title words cannot classify a genuine request as a test; explicit false wins.
Legacy simulation and environment evidence remains effective when migration defaults are present.
Tenant list responses omit internal summaries, internal actor/source data, and other database-only fields.
Pre-migration tenant reads do not reference migration-only columns.
A newly appended lifecycle event participates in latest-activity ordering.

phases.objective: Expose cursor-paged dry-run findings and guarded apply reconciliation that locks current rows and computes SLA from the effective post-lifecycle state.

e2e_journeys.terminal_outcome: The administrator receives lifecycle, SLA, visibility, relationship, milestone-evidence, assignment, and continuation findings; dry-run remains available before migration while apply remains schema-, confirmation-, and row-lock-gated.
steps: Authenticate the administrator and backend API key.
Inspect schema readiness and choose schema-safe milestone projections.
Calculate one keyset-paged finding batch.
Normalize dry-run SLA against the effective lifecycle outcome.
Return dry-run evidence and next_cursor without mutation.
Require typed confirmation and schema readiness before transactional apply.
Lock each current ticket row, recalculate lifecycle, then calculate SLA from that effective state before update.
Backfill durable first-response and triage timestamps from governed lifecycle events.
assertions: Dry-run never mutates tickets and remains readable before migration 1042.
Apply requires APPLY_SUPPORT_TICKET_INTEGRITY_RECONCILIATION.
Apply fails closed until migration 1042 is present.
A ticket closed by the lifecycle patch cannot be written as newly resolved with an SLA breach computed from its former open state.
Apply locks and rereads each target before mutation and fails closed if the target disappears.
Urgent unassigned and trusted test-ticket counts are explicit.
Reconciliation can continue beyond the newest 250 tickets through a stable keyset cursor.
Migration 1042 backfills existing lifecycle evidence and installs an idempotent single-statement milestone trigger.
Migration SLA backfill updates only changed SLA values and does not rewrite ticket updated_at.

phases.objective: Prove pre-migration read fallback, legacy evidence handling, and failure isolation through synthetic database contracts.

e2e_journeys.entrypoint: Integrity list and reconciliation services against a pre-migration schema contract
e2e_journeys.terminal_outcome: Tenant reads and admin dry-run remain available through schema-safe projections while creation and apply remain fail-closed; legacy test evidence and lifecycle-event activity stay observable.
steps: Return a schema preflight with all migration-1042 columns missing.
Build the tenant list query without any migration-only column reference.
Filter legacy simulation/test metadata without relying on migration defaults.
Build dry-run reconciliation with event-derived milestones and no migration-only column reference.
Include latest lifecycle-event time in ordering and cursor activity.
assertions: Pre-migration list and dry-run reconciliation do not raise unknown-column errors.
Legacy metadata can classify simulations despite default-like stored values.
Explicit legacy is_test false overrides simulation inference.
Lifecycle-event activity can move a ticket ahead of an older ticket-row timestamp.

phases.objective: Apply migration 1042 in an authorized non-production database and read back audited tickets.

planned_e2e_journey.entrypoint: Governed migration apply followed by dry-run and typed apply reconciliation
planned_e2e_journey.terminal_outcome: The canary database exposes required columns, dedupe claim table, and trigger, and audited records read back with corrected lifecycle, visibility, relationship, milestone, and SLA state.
steps: Apply migration 1042 under separate authorization.
Read schema readiness, dedupe_claim_table_count, milestone_trigger_count, and migration ledger evidence.
Run dry-run reconciliation through every cursor page, inspect findings, then apply approved corrections.
Verify audited ticket IDs and tenant inbox exclusion.

phases.objective: Promote the reviewed head, apply the migration, and verify customer-safe Production readback.

planned_e2e_journey.entrypoint: Production promotion, governed migration apply, and post-deploy reconciliation
planned_e2e_journey.terminal_outcome: Production reports exact SHA, migration evidence, serialized dedupe creation, corrected ticket states, legacy-test exclusion, customer-safe projection, lifecycle-event ordering, durable milestones, and lifecycle-aware SLA.
steps: Promote the reviewed exact head through the governed Production process.
Apply migration 1042 under separate authorization.
Run cursor-paged dry-run then approved typed apply reconciliation.
Verify exact ticket IDs, concurrent dedupe behavior, inbox ordering, customer-safe fields, SLA status, and tenant-safe readback.
